newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Moravske Chemicke restart aniline prod-paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech Moravske Chemicke restart aniline prod-paper.

text.p: Czech Moravske Chemicke Zavody a.s., one of Europe's biggest aniline producers, has restarted production after it was halted by heavy flooding, Czech daily Hospodarske Noviny reported on Tuesday.

MCHZ, which is part of the Chemopol Group, has also raised its original flood damage estimate by 15 million crowns to around 215 million crowns and now expects to post a 1997 loss of 70 million crowns after a 150 million crown gross profit last year, the paper said.

"The loss estimate comes from pessimistic assumptions ...moreover, the rate of the mark will have a big influence on the final result because we export 82 percent of our production to areas (which pay) in marks," MCHZ strategy and development director Jaromir Lubojacky was quoted as saying.
Aniline is a key component in polyurethane manufacturing.
Around one third of the Czech Republic was affected by heavy flooding in July which is estimated by the government to have cost the Czech economy around 60 billion crowns.
